questions.prompt: What does naming a file *.module.css do?

options.text: It scopes the class names so they can't collide with other components
It makes the styles apply globally to every page
It converts the CSS to Tailwind utilities
It disables the styles in production

questions.explanation: A CSS Module (*.module.css) has its class names automatically made unique, so styles are scoped to the component that imports them.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: import styles from './card.module.css'; then use className={______.card}.
questions.explanation: A CSS Module is imported as an object (commonly named styles); you reference classes as properties like styles.card.

questions.prompt: Which are good uses of global CSS (globals.css)? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Global CSS suits app-wide resets, tokens, and base styles. Component-specific styles belong in scoped modules to avoid collisions.

questions.prompt: Which limitation applies to inline style={{…}}?

options.text: It can't express pseudo-classes like :hover or media queries
It only works in Server Components

questions.explanation: Inline styles set individual properties but can't express :hover states or @media queries, so use them for dynamic one-off values.

questions.prompt: Match each styling approach to its scope or nature.
questions.explanation: Global CSS is app-wide, CSS Modules are component-scoped, Tailwind composes utilities in markup, and inline styles handle dynamic one-offs.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to style a component with a CSS Module.

items.text: Create a file named button.module.css with your classes

questions.explanation: Create the *.module.css file, import it as an object, then reference its scoped class names via that object.
